Versions, restoration and retesting

Unit 3 · Week 1 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Use the Unit 3 Week 1 student workbook and separate public teacher key at slides/practice/u3-week1/. Download the companion ZIP; extract before running. Python 3; Lesson 2 additionally uses the existing pygame/pygame-teaching-pack.zip and its pinned requirements. Read the unit3-fluency chapter and foundations workbook. Use fictional values and disposable history files only. No extra assessment or homework. Suggested 55-minute plans are untrialled; select one repair rather than completing every extension.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Week 1 practical resources

Follow the slide order; preserve each unaided response before opening its feedback.

Student workbook · Separate public teacher key · Download practical files · Four editable decks and resources

1. Versions, restoration and retesting

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use companion version exercise; all files are small fictional counter examples. This is hands-on recovery evidence, not a claim that a filename alone proves a backup. No Git account needed.

2. Retrieval: what is recovery evidence?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Think–pair–share

Elicit contents/location/version/test evidence. A copied filename or screenshot alone cannot establish that runnable earlier code was restored. Discuss separate destination and preserving working-v2 before the model.

3. A known baseline and a changed working copy

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model and prediction

Extract pack. seed-v1 contains rules.py,check.py,VERSION.txt. Run from that folder: python check.py prints source path,version1,expected2,actual2,PASS for[4,5,7]. Copy all three files to separate folders; leave snapshot-v1 unchanged. In working-v2 set MINIMUM=6,VERSION=2, expected=1 in check.py and VERSION.txt to2 with reason. Run current v2: expected1,actual1. Use school-approved file manager or shell; no destructive commands.

4. A usable version record

Suggested time: 8 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided documentation

Use version-log.csv. Record actual date/time,changed files,why,expected/actual,working/snapshot path. A filename v1 with edited contents is not the preserved v1. Teacher models one honest record; never supply fabricated classroom results. Optional hash or version control can supplement, not replace, actual restore/run evidence.

5. Restore to a separate folder

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent practical recovery

Close model. Students perform actual restoration, not a written plan. Do not overwrite working-v2. Restored v1 should report VERSION1,MINIMUM5,expected2,actual2,PASS. Check printed rules.__file__ points to restored-v1. If it points elsewhere investigate working directory/import path. If no computer available, plan on paper and mark actual restoration pending; it needs a later device check in existing support time.

6. Retest the preserved current version

Suggested time: 8 minutes

Instructional strategy: Regression check and explanation

Currentv2 threshold6 counts only7 from[4,5,7],so1; restoredv1threshold5 counts5and7,so2. A discrepancy must be investigated; do not edit the restored baseline to force a pass. Verify empty input0 for both and threshold boundary5(v1)/6(v2). Record separateactualresults and paths.

7. A partner checks the evidence

Suggested time: 7 minutes

Instructional strategy: Peer audit and optional extension

Partner checks log against files/run evidence,not just filename. This verifies the small example,not backup of an entire device or project. Optional extension: copy a snapshot to an approved separate storage location and retest; avoid assuming same-disk copies protect against drive failure. No mandatory cloud account.

8. Exit: restore, run and identify

Suggested time: 3 minutes

Instructional strategy: Practical exit demonstration

Allocated u3-l4: actual restoration and expected/reasoned result recorded; filename alone is insufficient. If working files overwritten, repeat safely into a separate destination with original preserved. Explain how documented versions support controlled returns in linear work and iterations. Use remaining issues to choose next retrieval.
